**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been working this land for 35 years. I know Quzhou soil and weather. My son works in the city now so I manage most of the farm work myself, sometimes hiring day labor at key times like cotton picking. My well gives me good water access which is important here because rainfall alone is never enough.

I will keep my wheat-maize rotation on the larger part of my land — about 8 mu. This is my most reliable income. Wheat goes in October and comes off in June, then I immediately plant maize. Cotton I will keep on the remaining 2.1 mu. I have been growing cotton a long time but it is getting harder to find people to help pick, and prices have been uncertain, so I do not expand it.

For seeds I will buy from the township supply shop — improved wheat variety that the neighbors also use, hybrid maize seed (郑单958 type), and a common cotton hybrid. I cannot read the labels well but the shop owner knows what I buy each year.

For fertilizer I apply compound fertilizer as base and then urea as top-dress. I learned the amounts by watching what my land produces. I water wheat four times — before winter freeze, at jointing, at heading, and during grain fill. Maize I water two or three times depending on summer rain. Cotton gets watered at flowering and boll setting.

For spraying, cotton needs the most attention — bollworm and aphids are always a problem. Wheat I spray once for weeds and once for rust or mildew near heading. Maize I spray for weeds after emergence.

I plough the cotton field each spring myself. For wheat I use rotary tillage since we switched a few years back — it is faster and saves fuel. After wheat harvest I use rotary tillage again quickly before planting maize because the window is short.
